narrative_before: This is a documented CTID emulation of menuPass (APT10), modelling the group's real MSP-subscriber-network intrusions. The plan is deliberately advisory and environment-agnostic: initial access is an assume-breach VPN/RDP connection with elevated permissions (abusing an MSP trust relationship), followed by tool ingress, discovery, credential access, lateral movement 'to systems of interest' via mounted shares/RDP/PsExec, collection/staging in the Recycle Bin, and exfiltration. The required infrastructure is specified only as roles (1 domain controller, 2 workstations, 2 servers) with no hostnames and no concrete source->destination lateral step between named hosts.

ambiguities: Documented emulation of the real menuPass/APT10 MSP campaigns.
The plan describes lateral movement only in the abstract ('to systems of interest') with role-only infrastructure (1 DC, 2 workstations, 2 servers) and no named source->destination hop.
drop_reason: No concrete lateral hop between identifiable hosts. The menuPass plan is advisory/environment-agnostic: it names infrastructure only by role and describes lateral movement abstractly ('to systems of interest'), giving no specific A->B edge to model, so it fails the entry + >=1 concrete hop requirement.
